## Overview

The **GPM DPR** (Dual-Frequency Precipitation Radar) product `2A-DPR` is the
Level-2 standard precipitation retrieval from the Dual-Frequency Precipitation
Radar aboard the **Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM)** Core Observatory,
a joint NASA/JAXA mission.  The DPR comprises two radars: Ku-band (13.6 GHz,
Full Scan) and Ka-band (35.5 GHz, High-Sensitivity scan), enabling
dual-frequency retrievals of precipitation rate, drop-size distribution, and
vertical structure.

The S3 bucket at `s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/GPM-DPR/` holds
V07C granule files for early 2026.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Satellite | GPM Core Observatory |
| Agency | NASA / JAXA |
| Instrument | Dual-Frequency Precipitation Radar (DPR) |
| Product | 2A-DPR, Algorithm Version 9 (V07C) |
| DOI | 10.5067/GPM/DPR/GPM/2A/07 |
| Swaths | **FS** (Full Scan, Ku+Ka, 49 rays) and **HS** (High-Sensitivity, Ka-only, 24 rays) |
| Along-track scans per granule | ~7 988 (`nscan`) |
| Height bins per profile | 176 (`nbin`) |
| Vertical bin spacing | ~125 m |
| Data format | HDF5 (`.HDF5`) |
| S3 bucket | `s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/GPM-DPR/` |
| Date range in bucket | 2026-01-19 – 2026-02-02 |
| Total granules | 88 |

---

## S3 bucket organisation

Files are arranged under a `{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/` hierarchy:

```
s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/GPM-DPR/
  2026/
    01/
      19/   ← 8 granules  (first available day)
      20/   ← 8 granules
      24/
      25/
      …
      31/
    02/
      01/
      02/   ← last available day
```

Each day contains 7–8 granule files, corresponding to roughly half the ~16
daily GPM orbits (the remaining orbits are apparently not included in this
collection).  Each granule covers one complete orbit (~95 min, global swath).
File size is ~760–790 MB per granule.

---

## File naming convention

```
2A.GPM.DPR.V9-{algver}.{start}-S{hhmm}-E{hhmm}.{granule}.V07C.HDF5
```

Example:

```
2A.GPM.DPR.V9-20240130.20260119-S021222-E034532.067482.V07C.HDF5
```

| Field | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `2A` | — | Processing level: L2A swath |
| `GPM` | — | Satellite |
| `DPR` | — | Instrument |
| `V9-20240130` | — | Algorithm version 9, dated 2024-01-30 |
| `20260119` | — | Observation date (UTC) |
| `S021222` | — | Granule start time: 02:12:22 UTC |
| `E034532` | — | Granule end time: 03:45:32 UTC |
| `067482` | — | Absolute granule number |
| `V07C` | — | File format version |

---

## File contents

Each HDF5 file contains two top-level swath groups and a metadata record:

```
/
├── AlgorithmRuntimeInfo     ← processing log string
├── FS/                      ← Full Scan swath  (Ku + Ka, 49 rays)
│   ├── Latitude   (nscan, nray_fs)
│   ├── Longitude  (nscan, nray_fs)
│   ├── ScanTime/  ← per-scan time components
│   ├── PRE/       ← pre-processing (surface clutter, echo flags, σ₀)
│   ├── VER/       ← vertical echo structure
│   ├── CSF/       ← column summary (bright band, precip type, hail flags)
│   ├── SRT/       ← surface reference technique (PIA estimates)
│   ├── DSD/       ← drop-size distribution
│   ├── SLV/       ← DSD-based retrievals (precip rate, water content)
│   ├── FLG/       ← quality flags
│   ├── TRG/       ← dual-frequency triggering
│   └── Experimental/
└── HS/                      ← High-Sensitivity swath (Ka only, 24 rays)
    ├── Latitude   (nscan, nray_hs)
    ├── Longitude  (nscan, nray_hs)
    ├── ScanTime/
    ├── PRE/, VER/, CSF/, SRT/, DSD/, SLV/, FLG/
    └── Experimental/
```

### Swath dimensions

| Swath | Along-track (`nscan`) | Cross-track (`nray`) | Height bins (`nbin`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FS` (Full Scan) | 7 988 | 49 | 176 |
| `HS` (High-Sensitivity) | 7 988 | 24 | 176 |

### Geolocation and time

| Dataset | Shape | dtype | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FS/Latitude` | `(nscan, 49)` | float32 | Footprint latitude (°) |
| `FS/Longitude` | `(nscan, 49)` | float32 | Footprint longitude (°) |
| `FS/ScanTime/Year` | `(nscan,)` | int16 | UTC year |
| `FS/ScanTime/Month` | `(nscan,)` | int8 | UTC month |
| `FS/ScanTime/DayOfMonth` | `(nscan,)` | int8 | UTC day |
| `FS/ScanTime/Hour` | `(nscan,)` | int8 | UTC hour |
| `FS/ScanTime/Minute` | `(nscan,)` | int8 | UTC minute |
| `FS/ScanTime/Second` | `(nscan,)` | int8 | UTC second |
| `FS/ScanTime/SecondOfDay` | `(nscan,)` | float64 | Seconds from UTC midnight |

### Selected science variables (`FS` swath)

| Dataset | Shape | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FS/SLV/precipRate` | `(nscan, 49, 176)` | mm/hr | Precipitation rate profile |
| `FS/SLV/precipRateNearSurface` | `(nscan, 49)` | mm/hr | Near-surface precip rate |
| `FS/SLV/precipRateESurface` | `(nscan, 49)` | mm/hr | Estimated surface precip rate |
| `FS/SLV/zFactorFinal` | `(nscan, 49, 176, 2)` | dBZ | Attenuation-corrected reflectivity (Ku, Ka) |
| `FS/SLV/precipWater` | `(nscan, 49, 176)` | g/m³ | Precipitable water profile |
| `FS/PRE/zFactorMeasured` | `(nscan, 49, 176, 2)` | dBZ | Measured reflectivity (Ku, Ka) |
| `FS/PRE/flagPrecip` | `(nscan, 49)` | — | Precipitation flag |
| `FS/PRE/height` | `(nscan, 49, 176)` | m | Range bin heights |
| `FS/CSF/typePrecip` | `(nscan, 49)` | — | Precipitation type (stratiform/convective) |
| `FS/CSF/flagBB` | `(nscan, 49)` | — | Bright-band detection flag |
| `FS/CSF/heightBB` | `(nscan, 49)` | km | Bright-band height |
| `FS/DSD/paramDSD` | `(nscan, 49, 176, 2)` | — | DSD parameters (D₀, Nw) |
| `FS/FLG/qualityData` | `(nscan, 49)` | — | Overall data quality flag |

Fill value: `-9999.9` (float32).

### Global metadata attributes

The file-level `FileHeader` attribute string contains key metadata:

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| `DOIshortName` | `2ADPR` |
| `AlgorithmVersion` | `9.20240130` |
| `SatelliteName` | `GPM` |
| `InstrumentName` | `DPR` |
| `StartGranuleDateTime` | `2026-01-19T02:12:22.166Z` |
| `StopGranuleDateTime` | `2026-01-19T03:45:33.596Z` |
| `GranuleNumber` | `67482` |
| `NumberOfSwaths` | `2` |

## Creating a VirtualZarr IceChunk store

The following demonstrates building an IceChunk store with virtual references
to three consecutive `2A-DPR` granules from 2026-01-19, reading directly from
their S3 URLs.

The store targets the `FS/SLV` sub-group (core precipitation retrievals) and
adds `FS/Latitude`, `FS/Longitude`, and a reconstructed `datetime64` time
coordinate from `FS/ScanTime`.  Spatial dimensions are named `nscan`
(along-track), `nray` (cross-track), and `nbin` (height bins).

### Setup

```{python}
import os
os.environ.setdefault("RUST_LOG", "error")

import io
import h5py
import icechunk
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
import obstore
from obstore.store import S3Store
from obspec_utils.registry import ObjectStoreRegistry
from virtualizarr.parsers import HDFParser
from virtualizarr.writers.icechunk import virtual_dataset_to_icechunk
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
```

```{python}
S3_BUCKET = "airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket"
S3_PREFIX = "JOIN/GPM-DPR/2026/01/19"
S3_REGION = "us-west-2"

# Three consecutive granules from 2026-01-19
GRANULES = [
    f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{S3_PREFIX}/2A.GPM.DPR.V9-20240130.20260119-S021222-E034532.067482.V07C.HDF5",
    f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{S3_PREFIX}/2A.GPM.DPR.V9-20240130.20260119-S034533-E051844.067483.V07C.HDF5",
    f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{S3_PREFIX}/2A.GPM.DPR.V9-20240130.20260119-S051845-E065155.067484.V07C.HDF5",
]

STORE_DIR = Path("../_data/gpm-dpr/icechunk-stores/2adpr_demo").resolve()
```

### Helper: read coordinates from a granule

`ScanTime` fields and lat/lon arrays are read eagerly per granule (~7 988 rows
each) and assembled into a `datetime64` time vector and 2-D lat/lon grids.

```{python}
s3_store = S3Store.from_url(f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/", region=S3_REGION)
registry = ObjectStoreRegistry({f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/": s3_store})


def read_dpr_coords(url: str) -> dict:
    """Read time, latitude, longitude from an FS swath granule."""
    key = url.removeprefix(f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/")
    buf = io.BytesIO(obstore.get(s3_store, key).bytes())
    with h5py.File(buf, "r") as f:
        st  = f["FS/ScanTime"]
        yr  = st["Year"][:]
        mo  = st["Month"][:]
        dy  = st["DayOfMonth"][:]
        hr  = st["Hour"][:]
        mi  = st["Minute"][:]
        sc  = st["Second"][:]
        ms  = st["MilliSecond"][:]
        lat = f["FS/Latitude"][:]    # (nscan, nray)
        lon = f["FS/Longitude"][:]   # (nscan, nray)

    # Build datetime64 from components
    iso = [
        f"{int(y):04d}-{int(m):02d}-{int(d):02d}T"
        f"{int(h):02d}:{int(mi_):02d}:{int(s):02d}.{int(ms_):03d}"
        for y, m, d, h, mi_, s, ms_ in zip(yr, mo, dy, hr, mi, sc, ms)
    ]
    time_dt = np.array(iso, dtype="datetime64[ms]")
    return {"time": time_dt, "latitude": lat, "longitude": lon}
```

### Open virtual datasets and attach coordinates

We open `FS/SLV` in multiple passes — one per distinct variable shape family —
because `phony_dim_*` indices are assigned per-dataset and variables with
different sizes on the same phony dimension would conflict.  Each pass uses
`drop_variables` to isolate one shape family, renames its dimensions, then all
passes are merged.  Dimension names are taken directly from the `DimensionNames`
attribute stored in the HDF5 file.

The 2-D lat/lon arrays are stored as regular data variables (not dimension
coordinates) because there is no single 1-D spatial axis.  Only `time` (along
`nscan`) is used as a dimension coordinate for `.sel()`.

```{python}
# FS/SLV variable families, grouped by shape
# (nscan, nray, nbin) — 3-D retrievals
VARS_3D   = ["DFRforward1", "epsilon", "flagSLV", "precipRate", "precipWater"]
# (nscan, nray) — 2-D surface/column quantities
VARS_2D   = ["binEchoBottom", "phaseNearSurface", "precipRateAve24",
             "precipRateESurface", "precipRateNearSurface", "qualitySLV"]
# (nscan, nray, nbin, nDSD=2)
VARS_4D_DSD  = ["paramDSD", "zFactorFinal"]
# (nscan, nray, nfreq=2) — per-frequency
VARS_3D_FREQ = ["piaFinal", "piaOffset", "sigmaZeroCorrected",
                "zFactorFinalESurface", "zFactorFinalNearSurface"]
# (nscan, nray, LS=2)
VARS_3D_LS   = ["precipWaterIntegrated"]
# (nscan, nray, nNUBF=3)
VARS_3D_NUBF = ["paramNUBF"]

ALL_VARS = (VARS_3D + VARS_2D + VARS_4D_DSD +
            VARS_3D_FREQ + VARS_3D_LS + VARS_3D_NUBF)

def open_slv_family(url, keep_vars, drop_others, dim_rename):
    """Open FS/SLV, keep only keep_vars, rename phony dims."""
    p = HDFParser(group="FS/SLV", drop_variables=drop_others)
    vds = p(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    return vds.rename(dim_rename)


vds_list = []
for url in GRANULES:
    parts = []

    # --- 3-D and 2-D (share phony_dim_0=nscan, phony_dim_1=nray, phony_dim_2=nbin) ---
    drop = [v for v in ALL_VARS if v not in VARS_3D + VARS_2D]
    p = HDFParser(group="FS/SLV", drop_variables=drop)
    v = p(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    v = v.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nscan", "phony_dim_1": "nray", "phony_dim_2": "nbin"})
    parts.append(v)

    # --- 4-D DSD: (nscan, nray, nbin, nDSD) ---
    drop = [v for v in ALL_VARS if v not in VARS_4D_DSD]
    p = HDFParser(group="FS/SLV", drop_variables=drop)
    v = p(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    v = v.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nscan", "phony_dim_1": "nray",
                  "phony_dim_2": "nbin",  "phony_dim_3": "nDSD"})
    parts.append(v)

    # --- per-frequency (nscan, nray, nfreq) ---
    drop = [v for v in ALL_VARS if v not in VARS_3D_FREQ]
    p = HDFParser(group="FS/SLV", drop_variables=drop)
    v = p(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    v = v.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nscan", "phony_dim_1": "nray", "phony_dim_2": "nfreq"})
    parts.append(v)

    # --- liquid/solid (nscan, nray, LS) ---
    drop = [v for v in ALL_VARS if v not in VARS_3D_LS]
    p = HDFParser(group="FS/SLV", drop_variables=drop)
    v = p(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    v = v.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nscan", "phony_dim_1": "nray", "phony_dim_2": "LS"})
    parts.append(v)

    # --- NUBF params (nscan, nray, nNUBF) ---
    drop = [v for v in ALL_VARS if v not in VARS_3D_NUBF]
    p = HDFParser(group="FS/SLV", drop_variables=drop)
    v = p(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    v = v.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nscan", "phony_dim_1": "nray", "phony_dim_2": "nNUBF"})
    parts.append(v)

    # Merge all shape families
    vds = xr.merge(parts)

    # Eagerly read coordinates
    coords = read_dpr_coords(url)

    vds = vds.assign_coords(
        time=("nscan", coords["time"],
              {"long_name": "scan time", "timezone": "UTC"}),
    ).assign(
        latitude =xr.DataArray(coords["latitude"],  dims=["nscan", "nray"],
                               attrs={"long_name": "latitude",  "units": "degrees_north"}),
        longitude=xr.DataArray(coords["longitude"], dims=["nscan", "nray"],
                               attrs={"long_name": "longitude", "units": "degrees_east"}),
    ).set_index(nscan="time")

    vds_list.append(vds)
    print(f"  {url.split('/')[-1]}: {dict(vds.sizes)}")
```

### Write to an IceChunk store (append per granule)

The HDF5 files use partial chunks at the end of `nscan`, so VirtualiZarr
cannot concatenate virtual arrays directly.  We write the first granule and
append subsequent ones using `virtual_dataset_to_icechunk`'s `append_dim`.

```{python}
shutil.rmtree(STORE_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
STORE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

config = icechunk.RepositoryConfig.default()
config.set_virtual_chunk_container(
    icechunk.VirtualChunkContainer(
        f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/", icechunk.s3_store(region=S3_REGION)
    )
)
repo = icechunk.Repository.create(
    icechunk.local_filesystem_storage(str(STORE_DIR)), config=config
)

for i, (url, vds) in enumerate(zip(GRANULES, vds_list)):
    session = repo.writable_session("main")
    if i == 0:
        virtual_dataset_to_icechunk(vds, session.store)
    else:
        virtual_dataset_to_icechunk(vds, session.store, append_dim="nscan")
    session.commit(f"Append granule {i}: {url.split('/')[-1]}")
    print(f"  committed granule {i}")

print(f"Store written to {STORE_DIR}")
```

### Re-open and inspect

```{python}
repo2    = icechunk.Repository.open(
    icechunk.local_filesystem_storage(str(STORE_DIR)),
    authorize_virtual_chunk_access={f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/": None},
)
ds = xr.open_zarr(
    repo2.readonly_session("main").store,
    consolidated=False,
    mask_and_scale=True,   # replace _FillValue (-9999.9 / sentinels) with NaN
)
print(ds)
print(f"\nTotal along-track scans: {ds.sizes['nscan']:,}")
```

The `time` coordinate enables time-based selection across all three granules:

```{python}
# Select a 15-minute window spanning the boundary between granules 0 and 1
window = ds.sel(nscan=slice("2026-01-19T03:40", "2026-01-19T03:55"))
print(f"Scans in window: {window.sizes['nscan']}")
print(window[["latitude", "longitude", "precipRateNearSurface"]])
```

## Visualizations

### Global swath: near-surface precipitation rate

The three granules together cover roughly a quarter of the globe.  We plot
`precipRateNearSurface` for the nadir ray (ray index 24, swath centre) as a
function of latitude and time.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning)

FILL = -9999.9

# Load nadir-ray near-surface precip for the full combined swath
prate = ds["precipRateNearSurface"].isel(nray=24).values   # (nscan,)
lat   = ds["latitude"].isel(nray=24).values                # (nscan,)
# Fill values already NaN via mask_and_scale=True; keep only finite values for LogNorm
prate = np.where(np.isfinite(prate) & (prate > 0), prate, np.nan)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 3))
sc = ax.scatter(lat, prate, c=prate, cmap="Blues", s=1,
                norm=mcolors.LogNorm(vmin=0.1, vmax=50))
plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label="Near-surface precip rate (mm/hr)")
ax.set_xlabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.set_ylabel("Precip rate (mm/hr)")
ax.set_title("GPM 2A-DPR FS — Near-Surface Precipitation Rate (nadir ray)\n"
             "3 granules · 2026-01-19 · ~02:12–06:52 UTC")
ax.set_ylim(0, 60)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Vertical curtain: precipitation rate profile

A curtain plot along the nadir ray for one granule.

```{python}
# One granule: 02:12–03:45 UTC
gran0 = ds.sel(nscan=slice("2026-01-19T02:12", "2026-01-19T03:45"))
pr    = gran0["precipRate"].isel(nray=24).values       # (nscan, nbin)
lat0  = gran0["latitude"].isel(nray=24).values

# Fill values already NaN; keep only positive values for LogNorm
pr = np.where(np.isfinite(pr) & (pr > 0), pr, np.nan)

# GPM-DPR range bins run top-down: bin 0 ≈ 22 km, bin 175 ≈ surface (~0 km).
# Passing height in descending order puts high altitude at the top naturally.
nbin = pr.shape[1]
height_km = np.linspace(22, 0, nbin)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 4))
pcm = ax.pcolormesh(
    lat0, height_km, pr.T,
    norm=mcolors.LogNorm(vmin=0.1, vmax=50),
    cmap="Blues", shading="auto"
)
plt.colorbar(pcm, ax=ax, label="Precipitation rate (mm/hr)", pad=0.01)
ax.set_xlabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.set_ylabel("Altitude (km)")
ax.set_title("GPM 2A-DPR FS — Precipitation Rate Profile (nadir ray)\n"
             "Granule 067482 · 2026-01-19 02:12–03:45 UTC")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Cross-track swath: near-surface precip for a 30-minute segment

```{python}
# 30-minute segment from granule 1
seg = ds.sel(nscan=slice("2026-01-19T03:45", "2026-01-19T04:15"))
prs = seg["precipRateNearSurface"].values        # (nscan, nray)
lats = seg["latitude"].values                    # (nscan, nray)
lons = seg["longitude"].values                   # (nscan, nray)
prs  = np.where(np.isfinite(prs) & (prs > 0), prs, np.nan)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 7))
sc = ax.scatter(
    lons.ravel(), lats.ravel(), c=prs.ravel(),
    s=1, cmap="Blues",
    norm=mcolors.LogNorm(vmin=0.1, vmax=50),
)
plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label="Near-surface precip rate (mm/hr)")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude (°E)")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.set_title("GPM 2A-DPR FS — Full-Swath Near-Surface Precip Rate\n"
             "03:45–04:15 UTC · 2026-01-19")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
